name: clef-guard
description: Has Cloudflare's Clef decision model judge each Bash, Write, Edit and WebFetch call (risk, kind of risk, whether it is read-only, whether it fits your request), asks you itself before risky or always-ask operations, and can approve plain reads for you.

accountId.title: Cloudflare Account ID
accountId.description: The account whose Workers AI runs Clef. Falls back to the CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID environment variable.

apiToken.title: Cloudflare API Token
apiToken.description: A token with Workers AI read permission, kept in secure storage. Falls back to the CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN environment variable.

model.title: Clef model
model.description: clef (27B, most accurate), clef-flash (9B, fastest and cheapest) or clef-omni (30B mixture-of-experts, also reads images, audio and video).

threshold.title: Ask threshold
threshold.description: Ask before an action when Clef puts its chance of being hard to undo or destructive at or above this (0 to 1).

tools.title: Tools to check
tools.description: Comma-separated: any of Bash, Write, Edit, WebFetch. Leave empty to check all four.

sendRequests.title: Send your recent requests
sendRequests.description: Send your last three prompts (redacted) with each call, so Clef can tell whether the action fits what you asked for.

autoApprove.title: Auto-approve plain reads
autoApprove.description: When Claude Code would show a permission prompt and Clef is at least 95% sure the action is read-only and on task, allow it without the prompt. Never applies to always-ask operations or to calls the rules deny.

alwaysAsk.title: Also always ask for
alwaysAsk.description: Comma-separated command prefixes that always need your yes, on top of the built-in ones (recursive rm, deleting a git repository, force push, wiping disks). Example: terraform destroy, kubectl delete
